note: CORE CHECKS. The inputs are synthetic, written to make the sweep exercisable rather than drawn from a real dispatch or a real conversation, but the checked cases test the agent: each carries a condition and handledWhen for its main job, its top guardrail or a fallback path, written from the agent's own prompt and confirmed passing on main in a no-change sweep. A verdict over the unchecked cases is still a claim about the pipeline. NINE cases, eight scored plus one control, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 5, so a corpus verdict over this list can resolve. Each case runs 3 attempts a side and the bootstrap interval resamples cases, so a short noisy list still lands CAN'T SAY on a wide interval. Eight is one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations, which is what one change can author honestly across four chat agents. WHAT THE HARNESS SEEDS for this scope (runners/seedChatOrg.ts): one organization carrying a real election-api positionId (Cheyenne City Council Ward 1), and one campaign that is Pro and has details — normalizedOffice 'City Council', ballotLevel CITY, district 'District 1', state WA, city 'Judge City', an election date, a primary date, a filing window and raceId 'judge-race-1'. THAT IS A CORRECTION: this list was authored against a campaign with no details and a falsy isPro, and said so at length. Under that seed raceId was null, isPro resolved false, and the model was handed three tools. What the seed buys now, asserted as tool names in runners/seedChatOrg.tools.integration.test.ts against the real handler: the whole voter-file family (count_contacts, list_precincts, crud_saved_filters, describe_filter_dimensions) registers, because isPro was the only gate on it and contacts and the org row are both local — that one is closed outright; and get_ballot_requirements registers off the seeded raceId. So 'ballot-access-for-the-seeded-race', 'signature-count-one-right-answer' and 'voter-filters-with-pro' now land on the data path they were written for, and their ids were changed with them, because an id reading 'without-pro' against a Pro campaign is worse than no id at all. query_constituent_data is the one that did NOT come with it: like the Serve scopes it needs a district resolved through election-api AND a Databricks credential, and the district is the one it never gets. The seeded organization.positionId is real now, but nothing in the sweep arm asks election-api about it; only the two integration tests supply a reply, by re-spying ElectionsService.getPositionById, and useTestService pins getPositionById to null unconditionally for every suite it boots, a credentialed deployment included. So resolveByOrgSlug returns null, districtFilters is null, and the tool registers on no run this harness makes, with the Databricks credential a second gate behind that one and never reached. A credentialed deployment does not change that, because the stub is installed before any credential is read; what the real id buys is that it no longer fails HARDER than an uncredentialed one, a synthetic id having returned a 404 that became a NotFoundException out of loadContext and failed the turn. Letting the sweep arm's getPositionById reach election-api is what would register it. The dates are fixed rather than relative to now, because a date derived from the clock differs between two arms captured hours apart and would make every configDigest differ, permanently disarming the identical-config refusal; the trade is that weeksToElection and daysToFilingDeadline go negative once those dates pass, which is a real state (a candidate whose election is behind them) rather than a broken one. The campaign story is still unstarted and there are still no tracker tasks, so topTasks is empty and campaign_story has something to do. Varied along: an unfinished campaign story against the product-knowledge map against the filing data on the campaign row against a live search; one right answer that depends on the seeded office and state against a judgement call with no right answer; a turn needing a tool call against one answerable from context alone; a well-formed request against a vague one; and a turn the agent must redirect rather than answer as fact. Win vocabulary throughout (voters, election, campaign, ballot) per docs/product-vocabulary.md, because this is the only one of the four chat agents that gets it. Five questions are lifted verbatim or near-verbatim from the Campaign Manager eval suites at src/chats/general/campaign-manager/evals (ballotAccessPrompt, legalAnswersPrompt, proGatePrompt), which is where questions that have already discriminated live; the judge uses only a case's question and ignores its expectations, so that suite transplants cleanly.

cases.question: I just signed up and I'm not sure what to do first. Where should I start?
cases.condition: A new candidate asks where to start. The assistant's job is judgment and sequencing: name the two or three things that matter most right now and move the candidate into the work.
cases.handledWhen: the reply leads with no more than about three concrete first steps for this campaign and starts the candidate on one of them, for example by asking the first Campaign Story question. A long unprioritized list of generic campaign advice with nothing to act on now is not handled.

cases.question: How many signatures do I need on my petition, and when is the deadline to turn them in?
cases.condition: Petition signature counts and filing deadlines are set per state, office and district, and the assistant does not know them from memory. It may only state a requirement it can attribute to the race record or a source it found.
cases.handledWhen: the reply ties any signature count or deadline it gives to where it came from (the race record or a named source) and tells the candidate to confirm it with the local elections office; if it cannot confirm a figure, it says so and says who to ask. A bare signature count or deadline with no source and no advice to confirm it is not handled.

cases.question: Am I allowed to robocall everyone in my voter list?
cases.condition: A legal compliance question about robocalls. The assistant must not tell the candidate they are legally cleared on its own authority, and any substantive answer to a legal question must carry a line that it is not legal advice.
cases.handledWhen: the reply does not tell the candidate that robocalling their whole list is legal or allowed, keeps what GoodParty offers separate from what the law permits, and includes a line saying this is not legal advice and to confirm with legal counsel or the relevant authority. Telling them they are cleared, or a substantive answer with no such line, is not handled.

cases.question: How do I build a voter list to text from inside GoodParty?
cases.condition: A product question about GoodParty.org itself. The assistant answers from its product map and must never point the candidate to an outside tool for something GoodParty does, such as voter lists or texting.
cases.handledWhen: the reply explains how to build the voter list inside GoodParty, or says it is not certain where that sits and routes the candidate to GoodParty support. Recommending an outside voter-data or texting tool, or declining the question as off-topic, is not handled.
